frames.narration: A cluster of 64 nodes. Node D has just crashed. Every node sends one ping per second to a random peer, so about one node per second happens to pick D. In round 1, node A does, and sends it a ping.

No ack comes back. A does not give up on one missing reply, which might be a lost packet on one link. It asks three other nodes to ping D for it, so the probe goes along three different network paths.
None of the three gets an ack either, and they report that to A. Four independent paths have failed, so A now doubts D. It does not yet say D is dead.
A marks D as suspect with incarnation 4 and starts a 7-second suspicion timer, which is about 4 x log10(64) seconds. D has until then to answer, which protects nodes that are only slow.

No special message is sent. The update rides on the pings and acks A sends anyway, and each node that learns it passes it on. The number of informed nodes roughly doubles every round, so all 64 know within about log2 64 = 6 rounds.

Meanwhile node F froze for 4 seconds in a garbage-collection pause starting at t = 2 s. It was suspected at t = 3 s. At t = 6 s it wakes up, receives 'F suspect, incarnation 7' on an incoming ping, and replies with a higher incarnation.

Alive with a higher incarnation overrides the suspicion everywhere, and the timers for F are cancelled. F was suspected for 3 seconds, less than its 7-second timeout. It is never declared dead, and none of its data moves.
D can never refute, because it is not running. At t = 8 s, 1 s plus 7 s, A's timer expires and A declares D dead. That update spreads the same way, and every node knows by about t = 14 s.

Each node removes D from its hash ring. Because of consistent hashing, only the keys D owned, about 1/64 or 1.6% of all keys, get a new owner, the next nodes clockwise. The other 98.4% of keys do not move.

Later a new node G starts. It knows only the address of a seed node, asks it for the member list, and receives the 63 live members in one exchange. G then announces that it has joined, and the news spreads on the probe messages.
